causalRedClassification.rootCause: BackendProcessHost performs physical fork before BackendOwnerRegistry's cross-process proper-lockfile owner claim is won. The later register conflict kills a loser only after duplicate physical execution already exists. During that conflict the losing registry refreshes to the winning record, while the losing child's exit path unconditionally calls markExited on the registry snapshot, allowing loser cleanup to terminalize the winner's durable owner record.
causalRedClassification.requiredOwningLayerChange: Reuse one existing owner authority only. BackendOwnerRegistry must provide a scoped non-blocking startup-admission boundary backed by its existing proper-lockfile arbitration and durable reread, rejecting an active contender before physical fork. BackendProcessHost must perform fork, PID/identity capture and durable owner registration inside that admission scope, preserve bounded containment before admission release on pre-registration failure, and terminalize an owner record only when the exiting child actually owns that durable claim. Existing register semantics remain compatible for direct registry callers; no forgeable caller flag may bypass the claim boundary.
